title: Finite and ramified compact-support coefficient arrows
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, their integer inclusion $A\to B$, and uniformizers $t,v$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use the completed and finite coefficient systems, geometric adjunctions, and compact-support image $Rp_*j_!$ [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. Define the tensor-composition and scalar-pullback comparisons by uniqueness of the left adjoints with their actual tensor-unit-normalized scalar restrictions [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Define the completed coefficient change by the actual completed inclusion. Define the proper scalar arrow as the scalar mate of the inverse of the normalized restriction/direct-image comparison, and the open scalar arrow as the scalar mate of the open-unit-normalized restriction square. For $e\in\mathbf N$, let the ramification condition be $\operatorname{map}(A\to B,(t))=(v^e)$. Define the retained quotient map $A/(t^n)\to B/(v^{en})$ by the actual quotient lift, its constant-sheaf change of coefficients, and its commutative square with the completed inclusion and quotient projections. Define tensor balancing for that square by the normalized tensor associators. For a compactification $c=(j,p)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and a completed coefficient complex $M$, define the finite comparison source and target at exponent $n+1$, and the arrow between them to be the proper mate followed by proper image of the open mate, evaluated on $M\otimes^L A/(t^{n+1})$. Finally define the finite pullback, open, separately derived image, and quotient-reduction presentation isomorphisms by their ordinary identity-on-sections direct-image comparison and their normalized adjunctions. No assertion of invertibility of the proper scalar arrow or of the compact-support comparison is part of this definition.
